text:
liam-eng: Heads-up — we flipped adaptive-microbatcher + short-circuit fallback into canary at 02:00 UTC. early numbers look good.
mike-bench: quick summary? numbers and which workloads?
liam-eng: p50 ~ same, p95 -10% on mixed bursty traffic, p99 -6%. cost/token down ~9% across helix-medium family. especially strong on mixed short+medium seqs.
yana-sre: any impact to error rates or retry storms?
liam-eng: no retry storm. one transient spike in requests when fallback threshold hit (we short-circuit to stable path) — circuit worked as intended. no OOMs.
mike-bench: bench command we used:```bash
./loadtest --model helix-medium --qps 800 --seq-mix 60:40: --dur 45m --batcher adaptive --fallback shortcircuit
```
liam-eng: baseline vs canary: - p95: 142ms -> 128ms; - p99: 320ms -> 301ms; - cost/token: $0.00048 -> $0.00044; - peak throughput +8% under burst.
ceo-alex: this is great — can we highlight in the next all-hands what enabled the win (runtime + policy change)? short blurb appreciated.
liam-eng: will draft a 2-sentence blurb: "Adaptive microbatcher reduces queuing for mixed seq distributions; short-circuit fallback prevents tail amplification during sudden bursts."
yana-sre: rollout plan?
liam-eng: staged rollout: canary -> 30% groups for 1h -> 60% for 2h -> full. health checks: p95, p99, 5xx rate, fallback-trigger-rate. auto-rollback if p95 regresses >7% for 10m.
yana-sre: adding dashboards/alerts: fallback-trigger-rate > baseline+3% (5m), p99 reg > baseline+7% (10m).
mike-bench: did we validate on quantized int4 paths?
liam-eng: yes validated on fp16/int8/int4 configs. no kernel-level changes required. change is in batcher + request routing.
deploy-bot: Canary roll started for group: helix-adaptive-canary. 30% -> running checks.
liam-eng: noted one small tweak: bump fallback threshold from 95th to 92nd percentile to reduce oscillation under very spiky patterns. documented in PR #4120.
ceo-alex: thanks team — please ping me when full is complete and share the short bench writeup. also add a note to release notes about cost improvements.
liam-eng: will do. follow-up: I’ll post the bench graphs and config knobs in #eng-runtime later today.
yana-sre: good job everyone :tada:
